newsitem.title: USA: Ind. bond plan funds $32.6 mln mortgage program.
newsitem.headline: Ind. bond plan funds $32.6 mln mortgage program.

text.p: Indiana Lt. Gov. Joe Kernan announced Tuesday that a $32.6 million debt issuance will make funds available for mortgage loans to first-time and current homeowners on Wednesday.
Funds for Indiana Housing and Finance Authority program were generated through a bond issuance last week that included both tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds and a taxable bond issue, Kernan said.
The blending of the two gave the authority additional capacity, while holding it "well-below market rate," Kernan said.

The authority makes three or four issuance of debt each year totalling about $150 million, Kernan noted. In February, the authority issued $35 million of bonds and it is expected to return to the bond market again in mid-summer, he said.
Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis purchased the issue last week, a first for a state housing agency, Kernan said.
The authority serves first-time homebuyers for the most part, but $8.6 million of the program will go to current homeowners through a one-time recycling of bond volume from an earlier issuance.
